title: ⭐⭐ Revision: reading an interview and answering it

questions.prompt: Your cousin cannot stop talking about football. Which sentence describes him in correct English?

options.text: My cousin is obsessed of football and knows every player.
My cousin is obsessed to football and plays it every Sunday.
My cousin is obsessed with football and talks about nothing else.
My cousin obsesses football and watches every match on TV.

questions.explanation: "My cousin is obsessed with football and talks about nothing else." is correct: obsessed travels with the preposition with, and the second half of the sentence shows what an obsession looks like. "obsessed to" and "obsessed of" copy prepositions from other verbs, and "My cousin obsesses football and watches every match on TV." uses obsess as if it took a direct object, which it does not in this sense.

questions.prompt: The last of the five questions on pocket money is about rights and favours. Which of these four answers makes pocket money a right?

options.text: Parents give it only to the children who work hard.
Parents give it when they can, and I always thank them for it.
Parents keep it and buy what the children need.
Parents owe it to a child: it is not a gift they choose.

questions.explanation: "Parents owe it to a child: it is not a gift they choose." makes pocket money a right, because a right is something owed to you and nothing is asked in return for it. "Parents give it when they can, and I always thank them for it." is the favour answer, and the thanking is its sign. "Parents give it only to the children who work hard." turns it into a reward for good behaviour, and "Parents keep it and buy what the children need." removes pocket money altogether.

questions.prompt: In its report your group must say what it thinks of Carol AND give the reason for it. Which sentence does both?

options.text: We believe that she has stayed simple, and some newspapers credit her with twenty million.
She gets eighty pounds each month and cannot touch her money yet.
We believe her simple, because eighty pounds is all she has to spend.
We believe that she has stayed simple, because eighty pounds is all she has to spend.

questions.explanation: "We believe that she has stayed simple, because eighty pounds is all she has to spend." does both: we believe that plus a whole sentence gives the opinion, and because plus a whole sentence gives the reason that holds it up. "We believe that she has stayed simple, and some newspapers credit her with twenty million." opens on the same opinion but follows it with a fact that supports nothing, and and is not because. "She gets eighty pounds each month and cannot touch her money yet." is two facts and no opinion at all: anybody could copy them out of the text without thinking. "We believe her simple, because eighty pounds is all she has to spend." has its reason but breaks the frame, since a verb of opinion needs that and a whole sentence after it, not a bare adjective.

questions.prompt: The newspapers present Carol and Max as a couple. What does the interview tell the reader about the two of them?

options.text: They have been friends since they were small.
They have decided to marry after her album.
They were a couple, but they separated before the album.
They are cousins who have never worked together.

questions.explanation: "They have been friends since they were small." is what Carol answers: the two of them have known each other since childhood and there has never been a couple to undo. "They were a couple, but they separated before the album." also refuses what the papers print, but it invents a love story the interview never mentions, and it is the trap. "They are cousins who have never worked together." gives them a family tie Carol never claims. "They have decided to marry after her album." simply repeats the story she denies.

questions.prompt: Carol answers a journalist with this sentence: "I'm not a skinny girl but I don't mind that." Which question was she asked?

options.text: You have your own house. What do you spend your money on?
Your mother travels with you. Is she the closest person to you?
Newspapers talk a lot about your looks. What do you think of that?
Some people say show business is a ruthless world. Do you agree?

questions.explanation: "Newspapers talk a lot about your looks. What do you think of that?" is the one: the answer describes her body and then gives her opinion of it, which is exactly the two halves the question asks for. The question about show business would be answered with an opinion on a trade, the question about spending with the name of a purchase, and the question about her mother with a yes or a no. None of those shapes fits an answer about being skinny.

questions.prompt: Your group is writing up the three things it dislikes about Carol. Which sentence belongs in that report?

options.text: The interview appeared in a British newspaper.
We do not like the way she talks about sending her parents away.
Carol Chapel was born seventeen years ago in a British town.
We think she is right to say that show business is a ruthless world.

questions.explanation: "We do not like the way she talks about sending her parents away." belongs there: the report collects the three things the group does not like, and this sentence names one precise point and judges it. "We think she is right to say that show business is a ruthless world." is an opinion too, and it is the trap: it is a thing the group likes, so it has no place in a list of dislikes. "The interview appeared in a British newspaper." and "Carol Chapel was born seventeen years ago in a British town." are facts, and a fact can be copied from the text by anybody without an opinion being formed.
